rows.source: NICE NG145 (laboratory reference range; consider treatment at TSH >= 10)
rows.note: NG145 gives no fixed TSH range and defers to the laboratory reference range; 0.4/4.0 is the range quoted in ATA 2014 (audit row 7b), used here as a stand-in. The >= 10 treatment threshold is NICE (audit row 7c).

rows.source: WHO 2024 anaemia cut-off, non-pregnant women 12.0 g/dL (men 13.0); no sex field, so 12.0 is used for all results; below the cut-off = CRITICAL (author decision 2026-10-19)
BCSH 2014: "<7 nmol/l (3 µg/l) is indicative of folate deficiency"; indeterminate zone "between approximately 7 and 10 nmol/l (3 and 4.5 µg/l)" (the guideline's own µg/L figures are used)
ROS < 30 nmol/L deficient, 30-50 may be inadequate (= 12 / 20 µg/L)

lab_reference_tier.note: Free T4 and free T3 have no guideline decision limit; they are classified against the reference intervals in spec/reference_intervals.json (SI Table A.2), never vote, and are used only in the thyroid rules. The other analytes listed here have no guideline decision limit and are not used in the analysis (decision D10, 2026-10-21). TestType_thresholds_and_categories.csv is no longer read.

decisions.D9: (a) verified guideline thresholds only; analytes without a guideline decision limit move to the reference-interval tier (author, 2026-10-19)
decisions.haemoglobin_cutoff: 12.0 g/dL for all results (WHO non-pregnant women); no sex field, men 12.0-12.9 are missed; stated as a limitation (author, 2026-10-19)
decisions.haemoglobin_tiers: below the WHO anaemia cut-off = CRITICAL; no ATTENTION tier for Hb (author, 2026-10-19)
decisions.tier_principle: CRITICAL = the guideline category that implies a diagnosis, a treatment decision, a severe grade or the highest risk class (e.g. HbA1c >= 6.5% diabetes; TSH >= 10 treatment; Hb < 12.0 anaemia; UKKA K >= 6.5 severe; NCEP TC >= 240 'high'); ATTENTION = the guideline's intermediate, at-risk, borderline or indeterminate category. Operators (lt/le/ge/gt) follow the source wording; see items/D9/D9_step1_thresholds.md
decisions.unit_conversions: glucose mg/dL = mmol/L x 18; 25(OH)D ug/L = nmol/L / 2.5; folate ug/L = nmol/L / 2.266. Where a guideline prints a limit in the stored unit, that figure is used (BCSH folate 3 and 4.5 ug/L).
